limitations: The checked-in policy authorizes zero hosted work. Published list rates are not verified account mappings or actual billing.

Every permitted job/attempt reserves its entire outer timeout, including startup, checkout, admission, cold provisioning, bounded command/transfer attempts, diagnostics, cleanup and reports. entryReserveSeconds requires a minimum envelope; checkout/guard have no separate aggregate deadline, so rejected-entry cost reserves the entire outer timeout, never just this minimum.
Disjoint reservations cover this exact source, workflow run, scope and policy maximum attempt only. They cannot be shared across runs, platforms or jobs.

Allowances apply independently to one workflow run. A documentation request and its separately dispatched certification are separate runs; repeated dispatches do not share an experiment-wide ledger or an aggregate cross-run spending cap.

Attempts beyond maximumRunAttempts fail at entry. Arbitrarily repeated rejected checkout/guard startup cannot be centrally bounded by this offline plan; provider budgets and authorized operator controls remain separate pending backstops.

Any applicable storage/transfer bound must cover the complete lifetime liability, all retries, cache provisioning and retained outputs. Unknown applicability rejects admission; a zero charge requires dated affirmative evidence.
A local maximum estimate is not an invoice or an immediate exact provider-enforced spending cutoff. Repository billing settings remain pending explicit authorization and verified read-back.
